speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with sudden-onset vertigo; to understand what is happening, please describe exactly what you are feeling. Are you experiencing a spinning sensation, or does the room feel tilted? Also, have you had any recent head trauma or noticed any new neurological symptoms like double vision or slurred speech?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

The description of sudden spinning vertigo lasting only a few minutes while getting into bed, followed by nausea and vomiting, and returning to baseline is classic for BPPV. Do you notice any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or imbalance that persists even when you are lying still?
